str:Agency.com:Name: SDMX
str:Agency.com:Description: SDMX is an initiative to foster standards for the exchange of statistical information. It is sponsored by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), the European Central Bank (ECB), the Statistical Office of the European Union (Eurostat), the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the Organization for Economic Co-Operation and Development (OECD), the United Nations (UN) and the World Bank.

str:Contact.com:Name: SDMX Secretariat
str:Contact.str:Role: Single entry point for external inquiries

str:Code.com:Description: Total forwards, FX swaps and currency swaps.

str:Code.com:Description: Total forwards and FX swaps.

str:Code.com:Name: Currency swaps
str:Code.com:Description: Contracts to exchange streams of interest payments in different currencies for an agreed period of time and potenital exchange of principal amounts in different currencies at a pre agreed exchange rate at maturity.

str:Code.com:Name: Forward rate agreements and IR swaps
str:Code.com:Description: Total FRA and IR swaps.

str:Code.com:Name: Forward rate agreements
str:Code.com:Description: Contracts where the rate to be paid or received on a specific obligation for a set period of time, beginning at some time in the future, is determined at contract initiation.

str:Code.com:Name: Interest rate swaps
str:Code.com:Description: Contracts to exchange periodic payments related to interest rates on a single currency (fixed for floating or floating for floating based on different indices).

str:Code.com:Name: Options
str:Code.com:Description: In FX derivatives segment, contracts that confer the right to buy or sell a currency with another currency at a specified exchange rate during a specified period. In interest rate derivatives segment, option contracts that confer the right to pay or receive a specific interest rate on a predetermined principal for a set period of time

str:Code.com:Name: Options sold
str:Code.com:Description: The right to purchase under OTC option contracts.

str:Code.com:Name: Options bought
str:Code.com:Description: The right to sell under OTC option contracts.

str:Code.com:Name: Credit default swaps
str:Code.com:Description: Contracts in which the protection buyer (risk shedder) pays a fixed periodic fee in return for a contingent payment by the protection seller (risk taker), triggered by a credit event on a reference entity. This is total value of all components.

str:Code.com:Name: Single-name
str:Code.com:Description: CDS where the reference entity is a single named entity, eg a corporation.

str:Code.com:Name: Multi-name
str:Code.com:Description: CDS referencing more than one name as in portfolio or basket credit default swaps or credit default swap indices

str:Code.com:Name: Index products
str:Code.com:Description: Multi-name credit default swap contracts with constituent reference credits and a fixed coupon that are determined by an administrator such Markit (which administers the CDX indexes and the iTraxx indexes).

str:Code.com:Name: Other instruments
str:Code.com:Description: Derivative products where decomposition into individual plain vanilla instruments such as forwards, swaps or options is impractical or impossible.

str:Code.com:Name: Total (all methods)
str:Code.com:Description: Sum of all executions methods.

str:Code.com:Name: Total (all maturities)
str:Code.com:Description: Sum of all maturities.

str:Code.com:Description: Between one and five years.

str:Code.com:Name: Over 5 years
str:Code.com:Description: More than five years.

str:Code.com:Name: Up to and including 1 year
str:Code.com:Description: Short-term.

str:Code.com:Name: Total (all risk categories)
str:Code.com:Description: Sum of all risk categories.

str:Code.com:Name: Foreign exchange
str:Code.com:Description: Contracts to exchange currencies in the forward market.

str:Code.com:Name: Foreign exchange including gold
str:Code.com:Description: Contracts to exchange currencies or gold in the forward market.

str:Code.com:Name: Interest rate
str:Code.com:Description: Contracts related to an interest-bearing financial instrument whose cash flows are determined by referencing interest rates or another interest rate contract.

str:Code.com:Name: Equity
str:Code.com:Description: Contracts that have a return, or a portion of their return, linked to the price of a particular equity or to an index of equity prices.

str:Code.com:Name: Commodities
str:Code.com:Description: Contracts that have a return, or a portion of their return, linked to the price of, or to a price index of, a commodity such as a precious metal (other than gold), petroleum, lumber or agricultural products.

str:Code.com:Name: Other precious metals
str:Code.com:Description: Any precious metal other than gold.

str:Code.com:Name: Credit Derivatives
str:Code.com:Description: Contracts in which the payout is linked primarily to some measure of the creditworthiness of a particular reference credit.

str:Code.com:Name: Other derivatives
str:Code.com:Description: Contract that do not involve an exposure to foreign exchange, interest rate, equity, commodity or credit risk.

str:Codelist.com:Name: Measure (notional amount, credit exposures, market values)

str:Code.com:Name: Outstanding - notional amounts
str:Code.com:Description: Nominal or notional amounts outstanding are the gross nominal or notional value of all deals concluded and not yet settled at the reporting date.

str:Code.com:Name: Gross positive market values
str:Code.com:Description: Gross positive market value of a dealer's outstanding contracts is the sum of the replacement values of all contracts that are in a current gain position to the reporter at current market prices (and therefore, if they were settled immediately, would represent claims on counterparties).

str:Code.com:Name: Gross negative market values
str:Code.com:Description: Gross negative market value is the sum of the values of all contracts that have a negative value on the reporting date (ie those that are in a current loss position and therefore, if they were settled immediately, would represent liabilities of the dealer to its counterparties).

str:Code.com:Name: Outstanding - gross market values
str:Code.com:Description: Sum of the absolute values of all outstanding derivatives contracts with either positive or negative replacement values evaluated at market prices prevailing on the reporting date. The term "gross" indicates that contracts with positive and negative replacement values with the same counterparty are not netted. Gross market values supply information about the potential scale of market risk in derivatives transactions and of the associated financial risk transfer taking place. Furthermore, gross market value provides a measure of economic significance that is readily comparable across markets and products.

str:Code.com:Name: Gross positive credit exposure
str:Code.com:Description: Corresponds to the market value after taking account of legally enforceable bilateral netting agreements (for contracts that have a positive market value).

str:Code.com:Name: Gross negative credit exposure
str:Code.com:Description: Corresponds to the market value after taking account of legally enforceable bilateral netting agreements (for contracts that have a negative market value).

str:Code.com:Name: Outstanding - gross credit exposure
str:Code.com:Description: Gross market value minus amounts netted with the same counterparty across all risk categories under legally enforceable bilateral netting agreements. Gross credit exposure provides a measure of exposure to counterparty credit risk (before collateral).

str:Code.com:Name: Herfindahl index
str:Code.com:Description: Measure of market concentration, defined as the sum of the squared market shares of each individual entity. The index ranges from 0 to 10,000. If only one entity dominates the market, the measure will have the (maximum) value of 10,000.

str:Code.com:Name: Notional amounts - bought
str:Code.com:Description: Notional amounts which the reporting bank has the right to purchase under OTC option contracts.

str:Code.com:Name: Notional amounts - sold
str:Code.com:Description: Notional amounts which the reporting bank has the right to sell under OTC option contracts.

str:Code.com:Description: Central counterparties are entities that interpose between counterparties to contracts traded in one or more financial markets, becoming the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer.
